reader_notes: Independent reading from the note text (tools/inventions/dump.ts, bars 1-32), checked bar by bar against transpositions of the opening worked out by hand; no published analysis consulted. x = the four-bar subject in the right hand, 1:1.5-4:4.5 (Eb D Eb F G Ab | F Eb F G Ab Bb | G C Bb Ab G Ab Bb Ab G F | Eb G Bb Eb5. C D Eb F Eb), whose first two bars are one rising unit stated twice a step apart (the 'head'). y = the continuous sixteenth-note countermotive that enters in the bass at 1:3.25 (Eb D Eb C D Bb C | Ab C Bb C Ab Bb G Ab | F Eb D C D Eb C D | ...) and runs to 4:4.75. opening.notes: The pair x + y is stated, then exchanged: a double-counterpoint opening (Dreyfus's ROTATE), not a canon. The exchange shifts the two lines by three octaves in all (x down 17 semitones, y up 19): invertible at the octave (compound).

notes: The piece is made of one paradigm, a four-bar pair x + y, stated five times (Eb, Bb, c, f, Eb), alternately in its original and exchanged disposition, plus three links built from x's head over y's figure. About 21 of 32 bars are members (1-8, 12-19, 27-31). The ending of x is varied in every member after the prime (leap to the seventh and fall a step) so that each segment hands on to the next key. Form: I divide at 12:1 and 23:1, giving three sections of 11, 11 and 10 bars, the second beginning with alpha in c: tripartite. The internal cadences are weak (only 23:1 is a clear PAC), so the division is unsure. Alternative: a ternary shape A (1-8, Eb-Bb-Eb) B (9-26) A' (27-32), i.e. rounded bipartite if one takes 23:1 (f) as the main internal cadence. The links 9-11 and 20-22 mirror each other (head rising above vs. falling below) but do not reproduce each other line for line, so they are not recorded as a paradigm. No canon: the imitation at bar 5 comes only after the whole subject, with the leader taking the follower's line.
review: Session lead, 12 October: the cadence at 12:1 checked against the notes (tools/inventions/cadences-check.ts): the bass is D3-Eb3-C3, not 5-1; relabelled 'IAC (weak)'.
